issues.legal_issue: The accused did not act in self-defence, and their possession of part of the land did not make the injured worker the aggressor.
material_facts: A large group entered a field where the worker was alone, and the evidence showed that the group assaulted him and the two officers who intervened.
The accused and their relatives had only trivial injuries, while the worker and officers had multiple injuries, mostly to the head and forehead.
The accused had been involved in a dispute at the field earlier that day, and the evidence indicated that they later went to the field and assaulted the worker.
Although the accused possessed part of the land, that circumstance did not establish that the worker had attacked them.
An independent witness testified that the accused removed their belongings from huts some distance from the field and then set the huts on fire.
issues.conclusion: The accused were the aggressors, and the claim that they assaulted the worker and officers in self-defence was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Whether conduct was in self-defence must be assessed from the circumstances and evidence, including the parties’ relative numbers and injuries. Possession of part of disputed land does not, by itself, establish that the other person was the aggressor. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this determination.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and (large_group_confronted_lone_worker and victims_suffered_multiple_head_injuries and accused_suffered_only_trivial_injuries)

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought an appeal challenging their criminal convictions.
predicates.large_group_confronted_lone_worker: A group substantially larger than the opposing party confronted a person who was alone.
predicates.victims_suffered_multiple_head_injuries: The person assaulted and those who intervened sustained multiple injuries, mostly to the head.
predicates.accused_suffered_only_trivial_injuries: The accused and their relatives had only trivial injuries.
predicates.self_defence_rejected: The court rejected the claim that the accused acted in self-defence.

issues.definition: When an appeal against conviction concerns a confrontation in which a large group faced a lone person and the victims suffered multiple head injuries while the accused suffered only trivial injuries, the court rejects the claim of self-defence.

issues.legal_issue: A false defence cannot establish the prosecution case, which must be assessed and proved independently.
material_facts: The accused claimed that the worker and officers had attacked them and that they had retaliated in self-defence.
The prosecution relied on direct testimony from the worker and the two officers who intervened.
The court found those witnesses credible and their testimony corroborated by their injuries.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution case was assessed independently of the defence, and the credible, corroborated prosecution evidence was sufficient to support the convictions.
issues.legal_principle: In a case depending on direct testimony, the falsity of the defence does not establish the prosecution case; the prosecution must prove its case independently. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and prosecution_case_depends_on_direct_testimony and direct_witnesses_found_credible and witness_accounts_corrobated_by_injuries

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought an appeal challenging their criminal convictions.
predicates.prosecution_case_depends_on_direct_testi: The prosecution relied on testimony from people who witnessed the incident.
predicates.direct_witnesses_found_credible: The court accepted the direct witnesses as credible.
predicates.witness_accounts_corrobated_by_injuries: The injuries sustained by the witnesses were consistent with and supported their accounts.
predicates.prosecution_case_independently_proved: The prosecution proved its case independently of the defence.

issues.definition: When an appeal against conviction rests on credible direct testimony corroborated by injuries, the prosecution case is independently proved rather than established merely by the falsity of the defence.

issues.legal_issue: The failure to call independent neighbourhood witnesses did not make the prosecution evidence unreliable in the circumstances.
material_facts: The accused argued that the prosecution had called interested witnesses while omitting independent people from the neighbourhood who had gathered at the scene.
The two officers who testified had no demonstrated connection with the worker.
The court found no credible evidence that an influential person had caused the police to fabricate the case.
An officer lodged the first report promptly, and it contained important elements of the account later given at trial.
issues.conclusion: The omission of independent neighbourhood witnesses did not undermine the prosecution case.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the credibility and circumstances of the witnesses actually called rather than treating the absence of independent witnesses as fatal. The absence of evidence of improper influence and the prompt report supported acceptance of the prosecution evidence. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this determination.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and independent_neighbourhood_witnesses_not_called and police_witnesses_had_no_demonstrated_connection_to_complainant and prompt_report_supported_account and no_credible_evidence_of_police_influence

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The accused brought an appeal challenging their criminal convictions.
predicates.independent_neighbourhood_witnesses_not_: The prosecution did not call independent people from the neighbourhood who were said to have gathered at the scene.
predicates.police_witnesses_had_no_demonstrated_con: The police witnesses had no demonstrated connection to the complainant that would make them interested in his favour.
predicates.prompt_report_supported_account: A report was made promptly and contained important elements of the account given later at trial.
predicates.no_credible_evidence_of_police_influence: The evidence did not credibly show that an influential person caused the police to fabricate the case.
predicates.omission_of_independent_witnesses_does_n: The absence of independent neighbourhood witnesses did not invalidate the prosecution evidence.

issues.definition: When an appeal against conviction involves omitted neighbourhood witnesses but the police witnesses had no demonstrated connection to the complainant, a prompt report supported their account, and there was no credible evidence of police influence, the omission does not invalidate the proof.
